393	def score_pair(
394	    *,
395	    buggy: Path,
396	    fixed: Path,
397	    symbol: str,
398	    properties: Sequence[Property],
399	    safety: SafetyPort | None = None,
400	    verify_for: Callable[[Path], VerifyPort] | None = None,
401	    render: HarnessWriterPort | None = None,
402	    work_dir: Path,
403	    unwind: int = DEFAULT_UNWIND,
404	    unwind_ladder: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
405	    max_len: int | None = DEFAULT_MAX_LEN,
406	    trigger: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
407	    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
408	    timeout_s: float | None = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S,
409	) -> PairScore:
410	    """Score `properties` on the (`buggy`, `fixed`) pair of `symbol`.
411	
412	    S0 runs on the clean version first and on the buggy one only if the clean
413	    passes; an excluded pair returns before any property is rendered or verified.
414	    Otherwise every property is rendered against each version (`render`, default
415	    `SemanticHarnessWriter`) and checked with `check_properties` unchanged, so the
416	    ladder, vacuity probe and HELD/VACUOUS rules are the check phase's own.
417	    `trigger` (scalar `name -> int`) enables the M4 absorption reading and is
418	    validated before any ESBMC call, as are `max_len` and the unwind ladder (derived
419	    as `check_source` does when `unwind_ladder` is None). `safety` and `verify_for`
420	    default to the real ESBMC bindings (`esbmc_safety_port`, `esbmc_verify_for`);
421	    the default S0 uses the same `max_len` as the property checks.
422	    """
423	    fixed_unit = Unit.from_path(fixed, symbol)
424	    buggy_unit = Unit.from_path(buggy, symbol)
425	    max_len = validated_max_len(max_len)
426	    ladder = (
427	        unwind_ladder
428	        if unwind_ladder is not None
429	        else default_unwind_ladder_above(unwind, max_len)
430	    )
431	    validated_ladder(unwind, ladder)
432	    pair_trigger, signature = _validated_trigger(trigger, buggy_unit)
433	
434	    safety = safety or esbmc_safety_port(
435	        max_len=DEFAULT_MAX_LEN if max_len is None else max_len,
436	        esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
437	    )
438	    s0_fixed = safety(fixed, symbol)
439	    s0_buggy = (
440	        safety(buggy, symbol) if s0_fixed.outcome is SafetyOutcome.PASSED else None
441	    )
442	    exclusion = exclusion_for(s0_fixed, s0_buggy)
443	
444	    def pair(
445	        excluded: Exclusion | None, scores: tuple[PropertyScore, ...] = ()
446	    ) -> PairScore:
447	        return PairScore(
448	            symbol=symbol,
449	            buggy_path=buggy,
450	            fixed_path=fixed,
451	            buggy_unit_id=buggy_unit.unit_id,
452	            fixed_unit_id=fixed_unit.unit_id,
453	            s0_fixed=s0_fixed,
454	            s0_buggy=s0_buggy,
455	            exclusion=excluded,
456	            scores=scores,
457	            trigger=pair_trigger,
458	        )
459	
460	    if exclusion is not None:
461	        return pair(exclusion)
462	
463	    verify_for = verify_for or esbmc_verify_for(
464	        timeout_s=timeout_s, esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin
465	    )
466	    writer = render or SemanticHarnessWriter(max_len=max_len)
467	    store = _FixedPropertySet(properties)
468	
469	    def run_on(unit: Unit, source: Path, subdir: str) -> PropertyCheckRun:
470	        return check_properties(
471	            unit,
472	            store=store,
473	            render=writer,
474	            verify=verify_for(source),
475	            work_dir=work_dir / subdir,
476	            unwind=unwind,
477	            unwind_ladder=ladder,
478	        )
479	
480	    fixed_run = run_on(fixed_unit, fixed, "fixed")
481	    buggy_run = run_on(buggy_unit, buggy, "buggy")
482	
483	    domain_verify = verify_for(buggy) if pair_trigger is not None else None
484	    scores = []
485	    for index, (prop, fixed_verdict, buggy_verdict) in enumerate(
486	        zip(properties, fixed_run.verdicts, buggy_run.verdicts, strict=True)
487	    ):
488	        discrimination, reason = classify(fixed_verdict, buggy_verdict)
489	        absorption, detail = _absorption(
490	            prop,
491	            buggy_verdict,
492	            pair_trigger,
493	            verify=domain_verify,
494	            signature=signature,
495	            path=work_dir / "domain" / f"p{index}",
496	        )
497	        scores.append(
498	            PropertyScore(
499	                prop,
500	                fixed_verdict,
501	                buggy_verdict,
502	                discrimination,
503	                reason,
504	                absorption,
505	                detail,
506	            )
507	        )
508	    return pair(None, tuple(scores))

511	def _validated_trigger(
512	    trigger: Mapping[str, int] | None, unit: Unit
513	) -> tuple[Trigger | None, UnitSignature | None]:
514	    if trigger is None:
515	        return None, None
516	    try:
517	        signature = extract_signature(unit.source_text, unit.symbol)
518	    except HarnessError as exc:
519	        raise ValueError(
520	            f"cannot read the signature to place the trigger: {exc}"
521	        ) from exc
522	    scalars = {p.name for p in signature.params if isinstance(p, ScalarParam)}
523	    missing = scalars - trigger.keys()
524	    if missing:
525	        raise ValueError(
526	            f"trigger must give a value for every scalar parameter of "
527	            f"{unit.symbol}; missing {sorted(missing)}"
528	        )
529	    for name, value in trigger.items():
530	        if name not in scalars:
531	            raise ValueError(
532	                f"trigger names {name!r}, which is not a scalar parameter of "
533	                f"{unit.symbol} (scalars: {sorted(scalars)})"
534	            )
535	        if not _INT_MIN <= value <= _INT_MAX:
536	            raise ValueError(f"trigger value for {name!r} is out of range: {value}")
537	    return tuple(sorted(trigger.items())), signature

540	def _c_int(value: int) -> str:
541	    return f"{value}ULL" if value > 2**63 - 1 else f"({value}LL)"
542	
543	
544	def _domain_program(signature: UnitSignature, trigger: Trigger, clause: str) -> str:
545	    ctypes = {p.name: p.ctype for p in signature.params if isinstance(p, ScalarParam)}
546	    lines = [f"#include <{header}>" for header in DEFAULT_INCLUDES]
547	    lines.append("int main(void) {")
548	    lines += [
549	        f"  {ctypes[name]} {name} = ({ctypes[name]}){_c_int(value)};"
550	        for name, value in trigger
551	    ]
552	    lines += [
553	        f'  __ESBMC_assert(({clause}), "{_DOMAIN_LABEL}");',
554	        "  return 0;",
555	        "}",
556	    ]
557	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

560	def _is_domain_violation(result: Violated) -> bool:
561	    """Only the clause's own assertion counts: undefined behaviour while
562	    evaluating it (division by zero, overflow) is a different violated property."""
563	    cex = result.counterexample
564	    return cex is not None and cex.violated_property.description == _DOMAIN_LABEL

567	def _absorption(
568	    prop: Property,
569	    buggy: PropertyVerdict,
570	    trigger: Trigger | None,
571	    *,
572	    verify: VerifyPort | None,
573	    signature: UnitSignature | None,
574	    path: Path,
575	) -> tuple[Absorption, str | None]:
576	    if (
577	        trigger is None
578	        or signature is None
579	        or verify is None
580	        or buggy.outcome is not PropertyOutcome.HELD
581	    ):
582	        return Absorption.NOT_APPLICABLE, None
583	    inputs = ", ".join(f"{name}={value}" for name, value in trigger)
584	    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
585	    unresolved: list[str] = []
586	    for index, clause in enumerate(prop.domain):
587	        program = path / f"clause{index}.c"
588	        program.write_text(_domain_program(signature, trigger, clause))
589	        match verify(program, unwind=1):
590	            case Violated() as violated if _is_domain_violation(violated):
591	                return (
592	                    Absorption.ABSORBED,
593	                    f"the triggering input ({inputs}) lies outside the domain "
594	                    f"clause {clause!r}: the property holds on the buggy version "
595	                    "only because its domain excludes the bug",
596	                )
597	            case Verified():
598	                pass
599	            case _:
600	                unresolved.append(clause)
601	    if unresolved:
602	        return (
603	            Absorption.UNDETERMINED,
604	            f"could not evaluate {unresolved!r} on the triggering input ({inputs})",
605	        )
606	    return (
607	        Absorption.IN_DOMAIN,
608	        f"the triggering input ({inputs}) satisfies the domain"
609	        if prop.domain
610	        else "the property has no domain",
611	    )

618	        violated = result.counterexample.violated_property.description

622	        "probe": verdict.probe.value if verdict.probe is not None else None,

708	def _property_from_obj(obj: object, unit_id: str, index: int) -> Property:
709	    where = f"property #{index}"
710	    if not isinstance(obj, Mapping):
711	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} is not an object")
712	    expression = obj.get("expression")
713	    if not isinstance(expression, str) or not expression.strip():
714	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} has no 'expression'")
715	    domain = obj.get("domain", [])
716	    if not isinstance(domain, list) or not all(isinstance(c, str) for c in domain):
717	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} has a 'domain' that is not a list of strings")
718	    try:
719	        kind = PropertyKind(obj.get("kind", PropertyKind.SEMANTIC.value))
720	    except ValueError as exc:
721	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} has an unknown kind: {exc}") from exc
722	    own_unit = obj.get("unit_id")
723	    unit = own_unit if isinstance(own_unit, str) else unit_id
724	    given_id = obj.get("property_id")
725	    property_id = (
726	        given_id
727	        if isinstance(given_id, str) and given_id
728	        else make_property_id(unit, kind, expression, tuple(domain))
729	    )
730	    return Property(
731	        property_id=property_id,
732	        unit_id=unit,
733	        kind=kind,
734	        expression=expression,
735	        status=PropertyStatus.CANDIDATE,
736	        provenance=_provenance_from(obj.get("provenance")),

743	    so a downstream report can aggregate per recipe and model."""
744	    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):

1	"""Bug-pair discrimination scorer (RFC-0007 M2 and M4, #394).
2	
3	Given two sources for one ``symbol`` -- a buggy version and its fixed twin -- and a
4	set of properties, report which properties *discriminate*: non-vacuously ``HELD``
5	on the fixed version and ``VIOLATED`` on the buggy one. A pair is *discriminated*
6	when at least one property does.
7	
8	Usable-pair filter first (RFC-0007 Tier 0). A bug pair measures a property set only
9	when the built-in safety checks (S0) cannot already see the bug, so S0 runs before
10	any property is rendered. A pair is *excluded*, with the reason, instead of scored
11	when S0 fails the clean version, S0 catches the bug, or S0 is inconclusive on
12	either. An excluded pair never reaches property checking.
13	
14	Verdict vocabulary: ESBMC emits no proof object. ``HELD`` means no violation found
15	up to the bound ``k`` (and ``length_bounds``) recorded on each verdict, never "holds
16	for all inputs". ``UNKNOWN``, ``VACUOUS``, ``ERROR`` or ``SKIPPED`` on either version
17	leaves that property's discrimination ``inconclusive``; it is never read as a pass
18	or as "does not discriminate".
19	
20	M4, domain absorption. When the pair carries a known triggering input (scalar
21	``name -> int`` assignments), a property that is ``HELD`` on the buggy version while
22	that input lies outside its domain holds there only because its domain excludes the
23	bug. Whether the input satisfies a domain clause is decided by ESBMC on a tiny
24	concrete C program (exact C semantics), not by re-implementing C in Python. Not
25	detected: a domain exclusion that is legitimate (undefined behaviour). The
26	usable-pair filter narrows this, because S0 passes the buggy version.
27	"""

210	        if self.exclusion is not None:
211	            return PairOutcome.EXCLUDED
212	        if not self.scores:
213	            return PairOutcome.EMPTY
214	        if any(s.discriminates for s in self.scores):

216	        if any(s.discrimination is Discrimination.INCONCLUSIVE for s in self.scores):

218	        return PairOutcome.NOT_DISCRIMINATED

221	    def discriminating(self) -> tuple[PropertyScore, ...]:
222	        return tuple(s for s in self.scores if s.discriminates)

225	        """Per-discrimination and per-absorption tallies, every key present."""
226	        discrimination = {d.value: 0 for d in Discrimination}
227	        absorption = {a.value: 0 for a in Absorption}
228	        for score in self.scores:

251	def reading_from_discharge(result: DischargeResult) -> SafetyReading:
252	    """Map an S2/S3 assessment to an S0 reading; only a pass or a real violation
253	    is decisive, everything else is inconclusive."""
254	    assessment = result.assessment
255	    match assessment:
256	        case Assessment.DISCHARGED_VERIFIED | Assessment.ASSUMED_VERIFIED:
257	            outcome = SafetyOutcome.PASSED
258	        case Assessment.VIOLATED:
259	            outcome = SafetyOutcome.VIOLATED
260	        case _:
261	            outcome = SafetyOutcome.INCONCLUSIVE
262	    return SafetyReading(
263	        outcome,
264	        result.label,
265	        assessment=assessment.value,
266	        assumed=assessment is Assessment.ASSUMED_VERIFIED,
267	    )

270	def esbmc_safety_port(
271	    *,
272	    max_len: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LEN,
273	    timeout_s: float = SAFETY_TIMEOUT_S,
274	    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
275	) -> SafetyPort:
276	    """S0 over the memory-precondition discharge (RFC-0003) plus signed overflow.
277	
278	    The sidecar harness materialises pointer arguments, so a pointer unit gets a
279	    meaningful memory verdict; a scalar unit gets the overflow check.
280	    """
281	
282	    def port(source: Path, symbol: str, /) -> SafetyReading:
283	        raw = sidecar_verify_port(
284	            timeout_s=timeout_s,
285	            esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
286	            extra_flags=(*SAFETY_FLAGS, f"-I{source.resolve().parent}"),
287	        )
288	        result = _discharge_precondition(
289	            source,
290	            function=symbol,
291	            max_len=max_len,
292	            timeout_s=timeout_s,
293	            esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
294	            raw_verify=raw,
295	        )

297	
298	    return port

325	def exclusion_for(
326	    fixed: SafetyReading, buggy: SafetyReading | None
327	) -> Exclusion | None:
328	    """The Tier 0 usable-pair decision, in a fixed precedence: a definite failure
329	    of the clean version, then any inconclusive reading, then the bug being caught."""
330	    if fixed.outcome is SafetyOutcome.VIOLATED:
331	        return Exclusion(
332	            ExclusionReason.S0_FAILS_CLEAN,
333	            f"S0 fails the clean version: {fixed.detail}",
334	        )
335	    if fixed.outcome is SafetyOutcome.INCONCLUSIVE:
336	        return Exclusion(
337	            ExclusionReason.S0_UNKNOWN,
338	            f"S0 is inconclusive on the clean version: {fixed.detail}",
339	        )
340	    assert buggy is not None  # S0 runs on the buggy version once the clean passes
341	    if buggy.outcome is SafetyOutcome.VIOLATED:
342	        return Exclusion(
343	            ExclusionReason.S0_CATCHES_BUG,
344	            f"S0 already catches the bug: {buggy.detail}",
345	        )
346	    if buggy.outcome is SafetyOutcome.INCONCLUSIVE:
347	        return Exclusion(
348	            ExclusionReason.S0_UNKNOWN,
349	            f"S0 is inconclusive on the buggy version: {buggy.detail}",
350	        )
351	    return None

354	def classify(
355	    fixed: PropertyVerdict, buggy: PropertyVerdict
356	) -> tuple[Discrimination, str]:
357	    """Discrimination of one property from its two verdicts (see module docstring)."""
358	    if fixed.outcome is PropertyOutcome.VIOLATED:
359	        return (
360	            Discrimination.NOT_DISCRIMINATING,
361	            "violated on the fixed version (a false alarm, or a bug there too)",
362	        )
363	    if fixed.outcome is PropertyOutcome.HELD:
364	        if buggy.outcome is PropertyOutcome.VIOLATED:
365	            return (
366	                Discrimination.DISCRIMINATES,
367	                "held on the fixed version and violated on the buggy one",
368	            )
369	        if buggy.outcome is PropertyOutcome.HELD:
370	            return Discrimination.NOT_DISCRIMINATING, "holds on both versions"
371	    return Discrimination.INCONCLUSIVE, _inconclusive_reason(fixed, buggy)

374	def _inconclusive_reason(fixed: PropertyVerdict, buggy: PropertyVerdict) -> str:
375	    parts = [f"fixed: {fixed.outcome.value}", f"buggy: {buggy.outcome.value}"]
376	    notes = [v.skip_reason for v in (fixed, buggy) if v.skip_reason]
377	    return "; ".join(parts + notes)

393	def score_pair(
394	    *,
395	    buggy: Path,
396	    fixed: Path,
397	    symbol: str,
398	    properties: Sequence[Property],
399	    safety: SafetyPort | None = None,
400	    verify_for: Callable[[Path], VerifyPort] | None = None,
401	    render: HarnessWriterPort | None = None,
402	    work_dir: Path,
403	    unwind: int = DEFAULT_UNWIND,
404	    unwind_ladder: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
405	    max_len: int | None = DEFAULT_MAX_LEN,
406	    trigger: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
407	    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
408	    timeout_s: float | None = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S,
409	) -> PairScore:
410	    """Score `properties` on the (`buggy`, `fixed`) pair of `symbol`.
411	
412	    S0 runs on the clean version first and on the buggy one only if the clean
413	    passes; an excluded pair returns before any property is rendered or verified.
414	    Otherwise every property is rendered against each version (`render`, default
415	    `SemanticHarnessWriter`) and checked with `check_properties` unchanged, so the
416	    ladder, vacuity probe and HELD/VACUOUS rules are the check phase's own.
417	    `trigger` (scalar `name -> int`) enables the M4 absorption reading and is
418	    validated before any ESBMC call, as are `max_len` and the unwind ladder (derived
419	    as `check_source` does when `unwind_ladder` is None). `safety` and `verify_for`
420	    default to the real ESBMC bindings (`esbmc_safety_port`, `esbmc_verify_for`);
421	    the default S0 uses the same `max_len` as the property checks.
422	    """
423	    fixed_unit = Unit.from_path(fixed, symbol)
424	    buggy_unit = Unit.from_path(buggy, symbol)
425	    max_len = validated_max_len(max_len)
426	    ladder = (
427	        unwind_ladder
428	        if unwind_ladder is not None
429	        else default_unwind_ladder_above(unwind, max_len)
430	    )
431	    validated_ladder(unwind, ladder)
432	    pair_trigger, signature = _validated_trigger(trigger, buggy_unit)
433	
434	    safety = safety or esbmc_safety_port(
435	        max_len=DEFAULT_MAX_LEN if max_len is None else max_len,
436	        esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
437	    )
438	    s0_fixed = safety(fixed, symbol)
439	    s0_buggy = (
440	        safety(buggy, symbol) if s0_fixed.outcome is SafetyOutcome.PASSED else None
441	    )
442	    exclusion = exclusion_for(s0_fixed, s0_buggy)
443	
444	    def pair(
445	        excluded: Exclusion | None, scores: tuple[PropertyScore, ...] = ()
446	    ) -> PairScore:
447	        return PairScore(
448	            symbol=symbol,
449	            buggy_path=buggy,
450	            fixed_path=fixed,
451	            buggy_unit_id=buggy_unit.unit_id,
452	            fixed_unit_id=fixed_unit.unit_id,
453	            s0_fixed=s0_fixed,
454	            s0_buggy=s0_buggy,
455	            exclusion=excluded,
456	            scores=scores,
457	            trigger=pair_trigger,
458	        )
459	
460	    if exclusion is not None:
461	        return pair(exclusion)
462	
463	    verify_for = verify_for or esbmc_verify_for(
464	        timeout_s=timeout_s, esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin
465	    )
466	    writer = render or SemanticHarnessWriter(max_len=max_len)
467	    store = _FixedPropertySet(properties)
468	
469	    def run_on(unit: Unit, source: Path, subdir: str) -> PropertyCheckRun:
470	        return check_properties(
471	            unit,
472	            store=store,
473	            render=writer,
474	            verify=verify_for(source),
475	            work_dir=work_dir / subdir,
476	            unwind=unwind,
477	            unwind_ladder=ladder,
478	        )
479	
480	    fixed_run = run_on(fixed_unit, fixed, "fixed")
481	    buggy_run = run_on(buggy_unit, buggy, "buggy")
482	
483	    domain_verify = verify_for(buggy) if pair_trigger is not None else None
484	    scores = []
485	    for index, (prop, fixed_verdict, buggy_verdict) in enumerate(
486	        zip(properties, fixed_run.verdicts, buggy_run.verdicts, strict=True)
487	    ):
488	        discrimination, reason = classify(fixed_verdict, buggy_verdict)
489	        absorption, detail = _absorption(
490	            prop,
491	            buggy_verdict,
492	            pair_trigger,
493	            verify=domain_verify,
494	            signature=signature,
495	            path=work_dir / "domain" / f"p{index}",
496	        )
497	        scores.append(
498	            PropertyScore(
499	                prop,
500	                fixed_verdict,
501	                buggy_verdict,
502	                discrimination,
503	                reason,
504	                absorption,
505	                detail,
506	            )
507	        )
508	    return pair(None, tuple(scores))

511	def _validated_trigger(
512	    trigger: Mapping[str, int] | None, unit: Unit
513	) -> tuple[Trigger | None, UnitSignature | None]:
514	    if trigger is None:
515	        return None, None
516	    try:
517	        signature = extract_signature(unit.source_text, unit.symbol)
518	    except HarnessError as exc:
519	        raise ValueError(
520	            f"cannot read the signature to place the trigger: {exc}"
521	        ) from exc
522	    scalars = {p.name for p in signature.params if isinstance(p, ScalarParam)}
523	    missing = scalars - trigger.keys()
524	    if missing:
525	        raise ValueError(
526	            f"trigger must give a value for every scalar parameter of "
527	            f"{unit.symbol}; missing {sorted(missing)}"
528	        )
529	    for name, value in trigger.items():
530	        if name not in scalars:
531	            raise ValueError(
532	                f"trigger names {name!r}, which is not a scalar parameter of "
533	                f"{unit.symbol} (scalars: {sorted(scalars)})"
534	            )
535	        if not _INT_MIN <= value <= _INT_MAX:
536	            raise ValueError(f"trigger value for {name!r} is out of range: {value}")
537	    return tuple(sorted(trigger.items())), signature

540	def _c_int(value: int) -> str:
541	    return f"{value}ULL" if value > 2**63 - 1 else f"({value}LL)"

544	def _domain_program(signature: UnitSignature, trigger: Trigger, clause: str) -> str:
545	    ctypes = {p.name: p.ctype for p in signature.params if isinstance(p, ScalarParam)}
546	    lines = [f"#include <{header}>" for header in DEFAULT_INCLUDES]
547	    lines.append("int main(void) {")
548	    lines += [
549	        f"  {ctypes[name]} {name} = ({ctypes[name]}){_c_int(value)};"
550	        for name, value in trigger
551	    ]
552	    lines += [
553	        f'  __ESBMC_assert(({clause}), "{_DOMAIN_LABEL}");',
554	        "  return 0;",
555	        "}",
556	    ]
557	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

560	def _is_domain_violation(result: Violated) -> bool:
561	    """Only the clause's own assertion counts: undefined behaviour while
562	    evaluating it (division by zero, overflow) is a different violated property."""
563	    cex = result.counterexample
564	    return cex is not None and cex.violated_property.description == _DOMAIN_LABEL

566	
567	def _absorption(
568	    prop: Property,
569	    buggy: PropertyVerdict,
570	    trigger: Trigger | None,
571	    *,
572	    verify: VerifyPort | None,
573	    signature: UnitSignature | None,
574	    path: Path,
575	) -> tuple[Absorption, str | None]:
576	    if (
577	        trigger is None
578	        or signature is None
579	        or verify is None
580	        or buggy.outcome is not PropertyOutcome.HELD
581	    ):
582	        return Absorption.NOT_APPLICABLE, None
583	    inputs = ", ".join(f"{name}={value}" for name, value in trigger)
584	    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
585	    unresolved: list[str] = []
586	    for index, clause in enumerate(prop.domain):
587	        program = path / f"clause{index}.c"
588	        program.write_text(_domain_program(signature, trigger, clause))
589	        match verify(program, unwind=1):
590	            case Violated() as violated if _is_domain_violation(violated):
591	                return (
592	                    Absorption.ABSORBED,
593	                    f"the triggering input ({inputs}) lies outside the domain "
594	                    f"clause {clause!r}: the property holds on the buggy version "
595	                    "only because its domain excludes the bug",
596	                )
597	            case Verified():
598	                pass
599	            case _:
600	                unresolved.append(clause)
601	    if unresolved:
602	        return (
603	            Absorption.UNDETERMINED,
604	            f"could not evaluate {unresolved!r} on the triggering input ({inputs})",
605	        )
606	    return (
607	        Absorption.IN_DOMAIN,
608	        f"the triggering input ({inputs}) satisfies the domain"
609	        if prop.domain
610	        else "the property has no domain",
611	    )

614	def _side_dict(verdict: PropertyVerdict) -> dict[str, Any]:
615	    result = verdict.result

617	    if isinstance(result, Violated) and result.counterexample is not None:
618	        violated = result.counterexample.violated_property.description
619	    return {
620	        "outcome": verdict.outcome.value,
621	        "k": verdict.k,
622	        "probe": verdict.probe.value if verdict.probe is not None else None,
623	        "length_bounds": dict(verdict.length_bounds),
624	        "reason": verdict.skip_reason,

679	class PropertySetError(ValueError):
680	    """A property-set file is not a readable list of properties."""

683	def properties_from_data(data: object, *, unit_id: str) -> tuple[Property, ...]:
684	    """Properties from decoded JSON: a list of property objects, or the object
685	    `propose --json` / `submit-property --json` print (its ``accepted`` list), or
686	    one with a ``properties`` list. Each needs an ``expression``; ``kind`` defaults
687	    to semantic, ``domain`` to empty, and a missing ``property_id`` is derived from
688	    the content under `unit_id`."""
689	    items = data
690	    if isinstance(data, Mapping):
691	        items = data.get("accepted", data.get("properties"))
692	    if not isinstance(items, list):
693	        raise PropertySetError(
694	            "expected a list of properties, or an object with an 'accepted' "
695	            "or 'properties' list"
696	        )
697	    return tuple(_property_from_obj(obj, unit_id, i) for i, obj in enumerate(items))

700	def load_properties_file(path: Path, *, unit_id: str) -> tuple[Property, ...]:
701	    try:
702	        data = json.loads(path.read_text())
703	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
704	        raise PropertySetError(f"cannot read property set {path}: {exc}") from exc
705	    return properties_from_data(data, unit_id=unit_id)
706	
707	
708	def _property_from_obj(obj: object, unit_id: str, index: int) -> Property:
709	    where = f"property #{index}"
710	    if not isinstance(obj, Mapping):
711	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} is not an object")
712	    expression = obj.get("expression")
713	    if not isinstance(expression, str) or not expression.strip():
714	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} has no 'expression'")
715	    domain = obj.get("domain", [])
716	    if not isinstance(domain, list) or not all(isinstance(c, str) for c in domain):
717	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} has a 'domain' that is not a list of strings")
718	    try:
719	        kind = PropertyKind(obj.get("kind", PropertyKind.SEMANTIC.value))
720	    except ValueError as exc:
721	        raise PropertySetError(f"{where} has an unknown kind: {exc}") from exc
722	    own_unit = obj.get("unit_id")
723	    unit = own_unit if isinstance(own_unit, str) else unit_id
724	    given_id = obj.get("property_id")
725	    property_id = (
726	        given_id
727	        if isinstance(given_id, str) and given_id
728	        else make_property_id(unit, kind, expression, tuple(domain))
729	    )
730	    return Property(
731	        property_id=property_id,
732	        unit_id=unit,
733	        kind=kind,
734	        expression=expression,
735	        status=PropertyStatus.CANDIDATE,
736	        provenance=_provenance_from(obj.get("provenance")),
737	        domain=tuple(domain),
738	    )
739	
740	
741	def _provenance_from(raw: object) -> Provenance:
742	    """The proposer attribution a `propose --json` run file carries, if any; kept
743	    so a downstream report can aggregate per recipe and model."""
744	    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
745	        return Provenance("", "")
746	
747	    def text(key: str) -> str:
748	        value = raw.get(key)
749	        return value if isinstance(value, str) else ""
750	
751	    return Provenance(
752	        text("prompt_id"), text("prompt_version"), text("provider"), text("model")
753	    )

1	"""The `check_properties` driver: which generated properties hold on real code (#66).
2	
3	The W2.5 *check* phase of the spine. Given a verification unit and the #62 store,
4	it loads that unit's candidate properties, renders each to a self-contained ESBMC
5	harness via #64, verifies it (escalating along the shared UNKNOWN k-ladder), and
6	records a per-property verdict (ADR-0009 D4: `held / violated / unknown`, plus
7	`error`/`skipped` so a bad harness or a deferred kind is never silently dropped —
8	CLAUDE.md "never silently pass").
9	
10	This is a *sibling* of `run_loop`, not a change to it: `run_loop` maps one source
11	to one terminal state and *fixes* on a violation; `check_properties` maps one unit
12	+ N properties to N verdicts and does **no** fixing (a `VIOLATED` property is a
13	result to record — the code violates that generated property). Mutation/kill-rate
14	*scoring* stays in the grading epic (#4); proposing stays in #65; the CLI/MCP
15	`propose` face stays in #44. This module owns only the check phase and its typed
16	result, `PropertyCheckRun`, which #4 consumes (its `held()` subset is the
17	mutation-kill candidate set) and #44 serializes.
18	
19	The driver is deterministic and effect-free in itself — verification, storage, and
20	harness rendering live behind the `VerifyPort` / `PropertyStorePort` /
21	`HarnessWriterPort` seams; the only I/O it performs is materializing each harness
22	to `work_dir` (the file esbmc reads) and emitting telemetry through the injected
23	sink (default `NullSink` = no-op).
24	"""

65	class PropertyOutcome(Enum):
66	    """Per-property verdict (ADR-0009 D4).
67	
68	    `HELD`/`VIOLATED`/`UNKNOWN` mirror the ESBMC verdict on the real unit;
69	    `ERROR` (a tooling/invocation failure) and `SKIPPED` (a reachability kind,
70	    deferred per ADR-0009 D2) are added so neither is silently coerced into a
71	    code verdict. `VACUOUS` (W3.4) is added the same way: ESBMC said VERIFIED but
72	    the post-call vacuity probe could not reach the assertion at that k, so the
73	    postcondition was never evaluated and the result is not a HELD.
74	    """
75	
76	    HELD = "held"  # Verified up to k
77	    VIOLATED = "violated"  # counterexample found
78	    UNKNOWN = "unknown"  # inconclusive after the ladder is exhausted
79	    ERROR = "error"  # esbmc failed (e.g. a harness that didn't compile)
80	    SKIPPED = "skipped"  # reachability kind, deferred (ADR-0009 D2)
81	    VACUOUS = "vacuous"  # Verified, but the post-call point is unreachable at k
82	
83	
84	@dataclass(frozen=True)
85	class PropertyVerdict:
86	    """One property's outcome on the real unit — the atom grading (#4) consumes.
87	
88	    `k` is the bound the verdict settled at (`None` when `SKIPPED`); `result` is
89	    the raw typed ESBMC result (`None` when `SKIPPED`); `harness_source` is the
90	    exact harness checked, kept as provenance so #4 can re-render it against
91	    mutants. `skip_reason` explains a `SKIPPED` outcome, a render-failure `ERROR`,
92	    or a vacuity-probe `VACUOUS`/`UNKNOWN`. `probe` is the post-call probe's
93	    reading (`None` when no probe ran: anything other than a Verified verdict);
94	    on a `VACUOUS`/probe-`UNKNOWN` outcome `result` is the Verified verdict
95	    / the probe's own inconclusive result respectively, both at `k`.
96	    `length_bounds` are the ``(param, max_len)`` caps the harness applied to
97	    buffer lengths the property's domain left unconstrained, so the verdict reads
98	    as scoped to ``len <= N`` rather than to every length (empty when none).
99	    """
100	
101	    property_id: str
102	    unit_id: str
103	    kind: str  # "semantic" | "reachability"
104	    outcome: PropertyOutcome
105	    k: int | None
106	    result: EsbmcResult | None
107	    harness_source: str | None
108	    skip_reason: str | None = None
109	    length_bounds: LengthBounds = ()
110	    probe: ProbeReachability | None = None
111	
112	    @classmethod
113	    def skipped(
114	        cls, property_id: str, unit_id: str, kind: str, *, reason: str
115	    ) -> PropertyVerdict:
116	        """A deferred property (a reachability kind, ADR-0009 D2): `SKIPPED`, no
117	        `k`/`result`/`harness_source`, carrying only the `reason` it was deferred.
118	        """
119	        return cls(
120	            property_id,
121	            unit_id,
122	            kind,
123	            PropertyOutcome.SKIPPED,
124	            k=None,
125	            result=None,
126	            harness_source=None,
127	            skip_reason=reason,
128	        )
129	
130	    @classmethod
131	    def render_failed(
132	        cls, property_id: str, unit_id: str, kind: str, *, reason: str
133	    ) -> PropertyVerdict:
134	        """A property whose harness could not be rendered (#64 fail-loud
135	        `HarnessError`): `ERROR` with no `k`/`result`/`harness_source` — esbmc was
136	        never invoked — carrying the render-failure `reason`. Distinct from an
137	        esbmc-error verdict (`settled` with an `Error` result), which does have a
138	        harness and a result.
139	        """
140	        return cls(
141	            property_id,
142	            unit_id,
143	            kind,
144	            PropertyOutcome.ERROR,
145	            k=None,
146	            result=None,
147	            harness_source=None,
148	            skip_reason=reason,
149	        )
150	
151	    @classmethod
152	    def settled(
153	        cls,
154	        property_id: str,
155	        unit_id: str,
156	        kind: str,
157	        outcome: PropertyOutcome,
158	        *,
159	        k: int | None,
160	        result: EsbmcResult,
161	        harness_source: str,
162	        length_bounds: LengthBounds = (),
163	        probe: ProbeReachability | None = None,
164	        reason: str | None = None,
165	    ) -> PropertyVerdict:
166	        """A property verified to a terminal `outcome` along the k-ladder: the
167	        settled bound `k`, the raw `result` (kept for #4 to re-render against
168	        mutants), and the exact `harness_source` checked. No `reason` — the
169	        outcome speaks for itself — except when the vacuity probe qualified it.
170	        """
171	        return cls(
172	            property_id,
173	            unit_id,
174	            kind,
175	            outcome,
176	            k=k,
177	            result=result,
178	            harness_source=harness_source,
179	            skip_reason=reason,
180	            length_bounds=length_bounds,
181	            probe=probe,
182	        )
183	
184	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
185	        """A JSON-serializable dict — the shape the grading harness (#4) reads."""
186	        return {
187	            "property_id": self.property_id,
188	            "unit_id": self.unit_id,
189	            "kind": self.kind,
190	            "outcome": self.outcome.value,
191	            "k": self.k,
192	            "harness_source": self.harness_source,
193	            "skip_reason": self.skip_reason,
194	            "probe": self.probe.value if self.probe is not None else None,

204	RunOutcome = Literal["held", "violated", "unknown", "error", "empty"]
205	
206	# What a `held` (and a `vacuous`) verdict does and does not show. The probe is a
207	# reachability witness, not a coverage claim, so it is stated wherever a probed
208	# verdict is reported (transcript footer, the vacuous reason, CLI/MCP docs).
209	VACUITY_LIMITATION = (
210	    "the vacuity probe shows only that some path reaches the post-call point at "
211	    "this k; it does not show that k covers every path (paths cut by "
212	    "--no-unwinding-assertions can still hide a violation)"
213	)

216	@dataclass(frozen=True)
217	class PropertyCheckRun:
218	    """The result of checking every stored property for one unit."""
219	
220	    unit_id: str
221	    verdicts: tuple[PropertyVerdict, ...]
222	
223	    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
224	        """Per-outcome tally; every `PropertyOutcome` key present (0 if none)."""
225	        counts = {outcome.value: 0 for outcome in PropertyOutcome}
226	        for verdict in self.verdicts:
227	            counts[verdict.outcome.value] += 1
228	        return counts
229	
230	    def held(self) -> tuple[PropertyVerdict, ...]:
231	        """The HELD subset — the mutation-kill candidate set the #4 seam grades."""
232	        return tuple(v for v in self.verdicts if v.outcome is PropertyOutcome.HELD)
233	
234	    @property
235	    def outcome(self) -> RunOutcome:
236	        """Core-owned, worst-outcome-wins summary across every checked property.
237	
238	        `violated` > `unknown` > `error` > `empty` (nothing semantically
239	        checked: no property stored, or every stored one was `skipped`) >
240	        `held`. A `vacuous` verdict (W3.4) is folded into `unknown`: the
241	        property's postcondition was never evaluated, so it is as inconclusive
242	        as a timeout and must never read as `held`; `counts()`/`verdicts[]`
243	        still tell the two apart. The one field a caller — the CLI's exit
244	        code, the MCP `check` payload, and the composed loop (`core/loop.py`) —
245	        reads instead of re-deriving verdict severity itself (issue #213): an
246	        adapter that recomputed this from `counts()` on its own could drift from
247	        the CLI's own policy, or (CLAUDE.md "never silently pass") miss that
248	        `empty` must not read as a clean pass just because it shares `held`'s
249	        exit code.
250	        """
251	        return self._outcome_for_counts(self.counts())
252	
253	    def _outcome_for_counts(self, counts: dict[str, int]) -> RunOutcome:
254	        if counts["violated"]:
255	            return "violated"
256	        if counts["unknown"] or counts["vacuous"]:
257	            return "unknown"
258	        if counts["error"]:
259	            return "error"
260	        checked = len(self.verdicts) - counts["skipped"]
261	        if checked == 0:
262	            return "empty"
263	        return "held"
264	
265	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
266	        """A JSON-serializable dict (unit id, counts, outcome, and every verdict)."""
267	        counts = self.counts()
268	        return {
269	            "unit_id": self.unit_id,
270	            "counts": counts,
271	            "outcome": self._outcome_for_counts(counts),
272	            "verdicts": [verdict.to_dict() for verdict in self.verdicts],
273	        }

276	class SemanticHarnessWriter:
277	    """The production `HarnessWriterPort`: a thin adapter over #64's writer.
278	
279	    Adapts the driver's `Unit`/`RenderedHarness` carriers to
280	    `render_property_harness`, the properties-domain recipe that owns the harness
281	    knowledge (parse the signature from the slice -> project the property onto a
282	    `SemanticSpec` -> render). Keeping the recipe in #64 (not here) is what lets
283	    `check_properties` stay a pure driver that need not know how a stored
284	    property becomes a harness. Fail-loud: a non-renderable unit/property raises
285	    `HarnessError` rather than emit a silent mis-harness. Non-semantic properties
286	    are skipped by the driver *before* this is reached (ADR-0009 D2), so `render`
287	    only ever sees semantic ones.
288	
289	    `max_len` (default `None`: no cap) is forwarded to the harness so a
290	    `(ptr, len)` buffer the property's domain leaves unbounded is capped at
291	    ``len <= max_len`` (#299); the caps actually applied ride back on the
292	    `RenderedHarness`. A negative `max_len` is a per-property render `ERROR`
293	    (the harness's own `HarnessError`); the Core faces reject it up front.
294	    """
295	
296	    def __init__(self, max_len: int | None = None) -> None:
297	        self._max_len = max_len

299	    def render(self, unit: Unit, prop: Property) -> RenderedHarness:
300	        harness = build_property_harness(
301	            unit_source=unit.source_text,
302	            symbol=unit.symbol,
303	            prop=prop,
304	            max_len=self._max_len,
305	        )
306	        return RenderedHarness(
307	            source_text=harness.source_text,
308	            length_bounds=harness.length_bounds,
309	            probe_source_text=harness.probe_source_text,
310	        )

313	def check_properties(
314	    unit: Unit,
315	    *,
316	    store: PropertyStorePort,
317	    render: HarnessWriterPort,
318	    verify: VerifyPort,
319	    work_dir: Path,
320	    unwind: int,
321	    unwind_ladder: tuple[int, ...] = (),
322	    sink: EventSink | None = None,
323	) -> PropertyCheckRun:
324	    """Check the checkable stored properties for `unit`, one verdict each.
325	
326	    Only non-terminal properties are checked (`CHECKABLE_STATUSES`): a terminal
327	    `ACCEPTED`/`REJECTED` row is settled, so it is never rendered, verified, or
328	    counted into the `counts()`/`held()` set grading (#4) consumes (#84).
329	
330	    For each remaining property: emit a start event, then — a reachability property is
331	    `SKIPPED` (ADR-0009 D2, never verified); a semantic property is rendered to a
332	    harness (written under `work_dir`, the file esbmc reads) and verified along
333	    `(unwind, *unwind_ladder)`, escalating on each `Unknown` and settling on the
334	    terminal verdict once the ladder resolves or is exhausted (never a silent
335	    pass). No fixing and no scoring happen here — a `VIOLATED` property is
336	    recorded as-is. Determinism: iteration follows `store.list_for_unit` order
337	    and `Event.seq` is monotonic.
338	    """
339	    ladder = validated_ladder(unwind, unwind_ladder)
340	    emit = EventEmitter(sink).emit
341	
342	    work_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
343	
344	    props = store.list_for_unit(unit.unit_id, CHECKABLE_STATUSES)
345	    emit("properties.loaded", detail={"unit": unit.unit_id, "count": len(props)})
346	
347	    def record_escalation(
348	        attempt: LadderAttempt, *, index: int, property_id: str
349	    ) -> None:
350	        if attempt.escalate_to is not None:
351	            emit(
352	                "unknown.policy.decision",
353	                index=index,
354	                detail={
355	                    "decision": "escalate",
356	                    "property_id": property_id,
357	                    "from_k": attempt.k,
358	                    "to_k": attempt.escalate_to,
359	                },
360	            )
361	
362	    verdicts: list[PropertyVerdict] = []
363	    for index, prop in enumerate(props):
364	        kind = prop.kind.value
365	        emit(
366	            "property.check.start",
367	            index=index,
368	            detail={"property_id": prop.property_id, "kind": kind},
369	        )
370	        if prop.kind is not PropertyKind.SEMANTIC:
371	            reason = "reachability harnessing deferred (ADR-0009 D2)"
372	            verdicts.append(
373	                PropertyVerdict.skipped(
374	                    prop.property_id, unit.unit_id, kind, reason=reason
375	                )
376	            )
377	            emit(
378	                "property.skipped",
379	                index=index,
380	                detail={"property_id": prop.property_id, "reason": reason},
381	            )
382	            continue
383	
384	        try:
385	            rendered = render.render(unit, prop)
386	        except HarnessError as exc:
387	            # #64 renders fail-loud on an un-renderable property (e.g. a
388	            # postcondition that dereferences a scalar-backed output). Record it as
389	            # a per-property ERROR -- CLAUDE.md "never silently pass" and this
390	            # module's own contract that a bad harness is never dropped -- rather
391	            # than crash the whole unit's run or hand esbmc un-compilable C.
392	            reason = f"harness render failed: {exc}"
393	            verdicts.append(
394	                PropertyVerdict.render_failed(
395	                    prop.property_id, unit.unit_id, kind, reason=reason
396	                )
397	            )
398	            emit(
399	                "property.verdict",
400	                index=index,
401	                verdict=PropertyOutcome.ERROR.value,
402	                detail={"property_id": prop.property_id, "reason": reason},
403	            )
404	            continue
405	        harness_path = work_dir / _harness_filename(unit.unit_id, prop.property_id)
406	        harness_path.write_text(rendered.source_text)
407	
408	        # Observation flushes each escalation before the next verification starts.
409	        final = climb_to_terminal(
410	            harness_path,
411	            verify=verify,
412	            ladder=ladder,
413	            on_attempt=partial(
414	                record_escalation, index=index, property_id=prop.property_id
415	            ),
416	        )
417	        outcome = _outcome_for(final.result)
418	        probed = _Probed(outcome, final.result, None, None)
419	        if outcome is PropertyOutcome.HELD:
420	            probed = _probe_post_call(
421	                rendered,
422	                harness_path=harness_path,
423	                verify=verify,
424	                k=final.k,
425	                verified=final.result,
426	            )
427	        verdicts.append(
428	            PropertyVerdict.settled(
429	                prop.property_id,
430	                unit.unit_id,
431	                kind,
432	                probed.outcome,
433	                k=final.k,
434	                result=probed.result,
435	                harness_source=rendered.source_text,
436	                length_bounds=rendered.length_bounds,
437	                probe=probed.probe,
438	                reason=probed.reason,
439	            )
440	        )
441	        detail: dict[str, Any] = {"property_id": prop.property_id, "kind": kind}
442	        if probed.probe is not None:
443	            detail["probe"] = probed.probe.value
444	        emit(
445	            "property.verdict",
446	            index=index,
447	            k=final.k,
448	            verdict=probed.outcome.value,
449	            detail=detail,
450	        )
451	
452	    run = PropertyCheckRun(unit.unit_id, tuple(verdicts))
453	    emit("properties.checked", detail={"unit": unit.unit_id, **run.counts()})
454	    return run

460	@dataclass(frozen=True)
461	class _Probed:
462	    outcome: PropertyOutcome
463	    result: EsbmcResult
464	    probe: ProbeReachability | None
465	    reason: str | None
466	
467	
468	def _probe_post_call(
469	    rendered: RenderedHarness,
470	    *,
471	    harness_path: Path,
472	    verify: VerifyPort,
473	    k: int,
474	    verified: EsbmcResult,
475	) -> _Probed:
476	    """Qualify a Verified verdict: is the post-call point reachable at the same k?
477	
478	    Runs the harness's probe twin once, at the bound the verdict settled at --
479	    never escalated, so it reads the very paths the HELD was decided on.
480	    REACHED keeps `HELD`; UNREACHABLE is `VACUOUS` (the postcondition was never
481	    evaluated); INCONCLUSIVE (the probe itself was UNKNOWN/ERROR, or fired
482	    without its label) is `UNKNOWN`; an Unknown/Error probe result is kept as
483	    the cause, but a stray probe `Violated` never replaces the property's own
484	    `Verified` -- the probe harness's trace is not its counterexample.
485	    A writer that supplies no probe also yields `UNKNOWN`: an unprobed Verified
486	    is never reported as HELD.
487	    """
488	    if rendered.probe_source_text is None:
489	        return _Probed(
490	            PropertyOutcome.UNKNOWN,
491	            verified,
492	            None,
493	            "no vacuity probe available for this harness; a Verified verdict "
494	            "is not reported as held without one",
495	        )
496	    probe_path = harness_path.with_name(harness_path.stem + PROBE_SUFFIX)
497	    probe_path.write_text(rendered.probe_source_text)
498	    probe_result = verify(probe_path, unwind=k)
499	    reading = classify_site_probe(probe_result, label=NON_VACUITY_LABEL)
500	    match reading:
501	        case ProbeReachability.REACHED:
502	            return _Probed(PropertyOutcome.HELD, verified, reading, None)
503	        case ProbeReachability.UNREACHABLE:
504	            return _Probed(
505	                PropertyOutcome.VACUOUS,
506	                verified,
507	                reading,
508	                f"vacuous at k={k}: ESBMC verified the harness but the post-call "
509	                "point is unreachable (unsatisfiable domain, or the call never "
510	                f"returns within k); {VACUITY_LIMITATION}",
511	            )
512	        case ProbeReachability.INCONCLUSIVE:
513	            return _Probed(
514	                PropertyOutcome.UNKNOWN,
515	                verified if isinstance(probe_result, Violated) else probe_result,
516	                reading,
517	                f"vacuity probe inconclusive at k={k}; held is withheld",
518	            )
519	        case _:
520	            assert_never(reading)
521	
522	
523	def _outcome_for(result: EsbmcResult) -> PropertyOutcome:
524	    """Map an ESBMC verdict to a property outcome (exhaustive over the union).
525	
526	    The final `assert_never` mirrors `state.py`'s `next_state`: adding a new
527	    `EsbmcResult` variant becomes a type error here, so no verdict is dropped.
528	    """
529	    match result:
530	        case Verified():
531	            return PropertyOutcome.HELD
532	        case Violated():
533	            return PropertyOutcome.VIOLATED
534	        case Unknown():
535	            return PropertyOutcome.UNKNOWN
536	        case Error():
537	            return PropertyOutcome.ERROR
538	        case _:
539	            assert_never(result)

541	
542	def _result_payload(result: EsbmcResult, k: int | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
543	    """The raw-result slice of a verdict's JSON shape — the settled `k` plus the
544	    shared `forseti.esbmc.result_to_dict` projection.
545	
546	    The check phase keeps the typed counterexample (`structured_cex=True`, the
547	    default): grading (#4) re-renders and diffs it against mutants, so it needs
548	    the structured trace, not just the raw text. `k` is this front-end's framing
549	    over the intrinsic verdict fields the projection owns.
550	    """
551	    return {"k": k, **result_to_dict(result)}

554	def _harness_filename(unit_id: str, property_id: str) -> str:
555	    """A filesystem-safe harness name per (unit, property), distinct + stable.
556	
557	    One file per property (mirrors `ProviderFixPort` writing one file per fix),
558	    so each property's harness is inspectable and never clobbers another's. The
559	    property id is already a content hash; the unit id is sanitized for the path.
560	    """
561	    unit = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", unit_id)
562	    prop = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", property_id)
563	    return f"{unit}__{prop}.c"

1	"""Deterministic mutants of one C function, for differential grading (W3).
2	
3	A property is scored by *holds on the real code AND breaks on mutants*; this
4	module produces the mutants. Five v1 operators rewrite tokens inside the target
5	function's body only -- the rest of the translation unit stays byte-identical --
6	and every emitted mutant has passed a validity check (by default: ESBMC's own
7	parser still accepts it and still defines the target). A mutant that fails the
8	check is dropped and counted, never scored.
9	
10	Mutation is token-level on a comment/literal-masked view of the source. Cheap
11	syntactic mutants may be semantically equivalent to the original; nothing here
12	claims otherwise -- it only guarantees they compile. Sites are taken from every
13	preprocessor arm, so a mutant of code the preprocessor drops (an inactive
14	``#if`` arm) is also equivalent to the original.
15	"""

144	def _relational(source: str, body: FunctionBody, op_index: int) -> Iterable[_Candidate]:
145	    for tok in body.tokens:
146	        flipped = _RELATIONAL.get(tok.text) if tok.kind == "op" else None
147	        if flipped is None:
148	            continue
149	        line = _line_col(source, tok.start)[0]
150	        yield _Candidate(
151	            op_index,
152	            tok.start,
153	            (Edit(tok.start, tok.end, flipped),),
154	            f"`{tok.text}` -> `{flipped}` at line {line}",
155	        )

158	def _is_binary(tokens: Sequence[Token], i: int) -> bool:
159	    if i == 0:
160	        return False
161	    prev = tokens[i - 1]
162	    if prev.kind == "num":
163	        return True
164	    if prev.kind == "id":
165	        return prev.text not in _NOT_AN_OPERAND
166	    return prev.text in (")", "]", "++", "--")

170	    tokens = body.tokens

173	        if swapped is None:
174	            continue
175	        if tok.text in ("+", "-") and not _is_binary(tokens, i):
176	            continue
177	        line = _line_col(source, tok.start)[0]
178	        yield _Candidate(
179	            op_index,

181	            (Edit(tok.start, tok.end, swapped),),

186	def _int_value(text: str) -> int | None:
187	    match = _INT_LITERAL_RE.fullmatch(text)
188	    if match is None:

190	    digits = match["body"]

192	        if len(digits) > 1 and digits[0] == "0" and digits[1].isdigit():
193	            return int(digits, 8)
194	        return int(digits, 0)
195	    except ValueError:

199	def _const(source: str, body: FunctionBody, op_index: int) -> Iterable[_Candidate]:

204	        if value is None:

207	        for sign, delta in (("+", 1), ("-", -1)):
208	            yield _Candidate(
209	                op_index,

212	                f"`{tok.text}` -> `{value + delta}` at line {line}",

216	def _guard_end(tokens: Sequence[Token], i: int) -> int | None:
217	    """Token index ending the ``if (c) return ...;`` guard at `i`, else ``None``."""
218	    if tokens[i].text != "if" or i + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[i + 1].text != "(":
219	        return None
220	    close = match_close(tokens, i + 1, "(", ")")
221	    if close is None or close + 1 >= len(tokens):
222	        return None
223	    j = close + 1
224	    braced = tokens[j].text == "{"
225	    if braced:
226	        j += 1
227	    if j >= len(tokens) or tokens[j].text != "return":
228	        return None
229	    end = statement_end(tokens, j)
230	    if end is None:
231	        return None
232	    if braced:
233	        end += 1
234	        if end >= len(tokens) or tokens[end].text != "}":
235	            return None
236	    return end

239	def _guard_drop(source: str, body: FunctionBody, op_index: int) -> Iterable[_Candidate]:
240	    tokens = body.tokens
241	    for i, tok in enumerate(tokens):
242	        end = _guard_end(tokens, i)
243	        if end is None:
244	            continue
245	        if i > 0 and tokens[i - 1].text == "else":
246	            continue
247	        if end + 1 < len(tokens) and tokens[end + 1].text == "else":
248	            continue
249	        span_end = tokens[end].end
250	        if _DIRECTIVE_LINE_RE.search(source, tok.start, span_end):
251	            continue
252	        standalone = i == 0 or tokens[i - 1].text in ("{", ";", "}")
253	        text = " ".join(source[tok.start : span_end].split())
254	        if len(text) > _GUARD_PREVIEW:
255	            text = text[: _GUARD_PREVIEW - 3] + "..."
256	        line = _line_col(source, tok.start)[0]
257	        yield _Candidate(
258	            op_index,
259	            tok.start,
260	            (Edit(tok.start, span_end, "" if standalone else ";"),),
261	            f"drop guard `{text}` at line {line}",
262	        )

265	def _havoc_candidate(
266	    source: str,
267	    body: FunctionBody,
268	    op_index: int,
269	    tokens: Sequence[Token],
270	    value_start: int,
271	    ctype: str,
272	    what: str,
273	) -> _Candidate | None:
274	    """Replace the expression statement starting at token `value_start` with a
275	    nondet call of `ctype`, or ``None`` if it is not a plain, non-havoc one."""
276	    end = statement_end(tokens, value_start)
277	    if end is None or end == value_start:
278	        return None
279	    call = f"{_nondet_name(ctype)}()"
280	    start, stop = tokens[value_start].start, tokens[end - 1].end
281	    if source[start:stop] == call:
282	        return None
283	    line = _line_col(source, start)[0]
284	    return _Candidate(
285	        op_index,
286	        start,
287	        (Edit(start, stop, call), _prototype(ctype, body.open_brace + 1)),
288	        f"havoc {what} with `{call}` at line {line}",

313	    tokens = body.tokens

321	            name = tok.text

324	        if eq is None or eq >= len(tokens) or tokens[eq].text != "=":

328	            body,
329	            op_index,

344	_GENERATORS: dict[str, Callable[[str, FunctionBody, int], Iterable[_Candidate]]] = {

353	def _apply(source: str, edits: Sequence[Edit]) -> str:
354	    out = source
355	    for edit in sorted(edits, key=lambda e: (e.start, e.end), reverse=True):
356	        out = out[: edit.start] + edit.text + out[edit.end :]

360	def candidates(
361	    source: str, body: FunctionBody, operators: Iterable[str]
362	) -> list[_Candidate]:
363	    wanted = set(operators)
364	    unknown = wanted - set(OPERATORS)
365	    if unknown:
366	        raise ValueError(f"unknown mutation operator(s): {sorted(unknown)}")
367	    found: list[_Candidate] = []
368	    for index, name in enumerate(OPERATORS):
369	        if name in wanted:
370	            found.extend(_GENERATORS[name](source, body, index))
371	    found.sort(key=lambda c: (c.offset, c.op_index))
372	    return found

375	def _assign_ids(source: str, cands: Sequence[_Candidate]) -> list[MutantId]:
376	    """Ids over *all* candidates, so a mutant's id does not depend on the cap."""
377	    ordinals: dict[tuple[str, int, int], int] = {}
378	    ids: list[MutantId] = []
379	    for cand in cands:
380	        line, column = _line_col(source, cand.offset)
381	        name = OPERATORS[cand.op_index]
382	        ordinal = ordinals.get((name, line, column), 0)
383	        ordinals[(name, line, column)] = ordinal + 1
384	        ids.append(MutantId(name, line, column, ordinal))
385	    return ids

390	    symbol: str,
391	    *,
392	    validate: Callable[[str], bool],
393	    operators: Iterable[str] = OPERATORS,
394	    cap: int | None = None,
395	    seed: int = 0,
396	) -> MutationResult:
397	    """Mutants of `symbol`'s body in `source`, in (offset, operator order) order.
398	
399	    `validate` is the validity oracle: a mutant it rejects is dropped and counted
400	    in `MutationResult.dropped`, never returned. With `cap`, candidates are tried
401	    in a `seed`-fixed random order until `cap` valid mutants are collected (so a
402	    cap spares the validator, the expensive step), then returned in canonical
403	    order; `dropped` then counts only the candidates tried. The same source,
404	    operator set, cap and seed give the same mutants in the same order.
405	    """
406	    try:
407	        body = locate_body(source, symbol)
408	    except BodyNotFound as exc:
409	        raise MutationError(str(exc)) from exc
410	    cands = candidates(source, body, operators)
411	    order = list(range(len(cands)))
412	    if cap is not None:
413	        random.Random(seed).shuffle(order)
414	    kept: dict[int, str] = {}
415	    dropped = 0
416	    for idx in order:
417	        if cap is not None and len(kept) >= cap:
418	            break
419	        mutated = _apply(source, cands[idx].edits)
420	        if validate(mutated):
421	            kept[idx] = mutated
422	        else:
423	            dropped += 1
424	    ids = _assign_ids(source, cands)
425	    mutants = [
426	        Mutant(ids[idx], kept[idx], cands[idx].description, cands[idx].edits)
427	        for idx in sorted(kept)
428	    ]
429	    return MutationResult(tuple(mutants), dropped)
430	
431	
432	def esbmc_validator(
433	    symbol: str,
434	    *,
435	    suffix: str = ".c",
436	    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
437	    timeout_s: float = 30.0,
438	    extra_flags: Sequence[str] = (),
439	) -> Callable[[str], bool]:
440	    """A validity oracle: ESBMC parses the source and it still defines `symbol`."""
441	    if shutil.which(esbmc_bin) is None:
442	        raise MutationError(f"esbmc binary not found: {esbmc_bin}")
443	
444	    def validate(source: str) -> bool:
445	        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="forseti-mutant-") as tmp:
446	            path = Path(tmp) / f"mutant{suffix}"
447	            path.write_text(source)
448	            try:
449	                units = list_units(
450	                    path,
451	                    esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
452	                    timeout_s=timeout_s,
453	                    extra_flags=extra_flags,
454	                )
455	            except ListUnitsError as exc:
456	                if isinstance(exc.__cause__, OSError | subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
457	                    raise MutationError(f"cannot run {esbmc_bin}: {exc}") from exc
458	                return False
459	        return any(unit.name == symbol for unit in units)
460	
461	    return validate
462	
463	
464	def mutate_function(
465	    path: Path,
466	    symbol: str,
467	    *,
468	    operators: Iterable[str] = OPERATORS,
469	    cap: int | None = None,
470	    seed: int = 0,
471	    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
472	    timeout_s: float = 30.0,
473	    extra_flags: Sequence[str] = (),
474	) -> MutationResult:
475	    """`generate_mutants` for the unit ``path::symbol``, validated with ESBMC.
476	
477	    Raises `MutationError` if the unmutated file does not itself parse, since
478	    every mutant would then be dropped and the count would mean nothing.
479	    """
480	    source = path.read_text()
481	    validate = esbmc_validator(
482	        symbol,
483	        suffix=path.suffix or ".c",
484	        esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
485	        timeout_s=timeout_s,
486	        extra_flags=(f"-I{path.resolve().parent}", *extra_flags),
487	    )
488	    if not validate(source):
489	        raise MutationError(f"{path}: the original does not parse as defining {symbol}")
490	    return generate_mutants(
491	        source, symbol, validate=validate, operators=operators, cap=cap, seed=seed
492	    )

1	"""The `check_properties` driver: which generated properties hold on real code (#66).
2	
3	The W2.5 *check* phase of the spine. Given a verification unit and the #62 store,
4	it loads that unit's candidate properties, renders each to a self-contained ESBMC
5	harness via #64, verifies it (escalating along the shared UNKNOWN k-ladder), and
6	records a per-property verdict (ADR-0009 D4: `held / violated / unknown`, plus
7	`error`/`skipped` so a bad harness or a deferred kind is never silently dropped —
8	CLAUDE.md "never silently pass").
9	
10	This is a *sibling* of `run_loop`, not a change to it: `run_loop` maps one source
11	to one terminal state and *fixes* on a violation; `check_properties` maps one unit
12	+ N properties to N verdicts and does **no** fixing (a `VIOLATED` property is a
13	result to record — the code violates that generated property). Mutation/kill-rate
14	*scoring* stays in the grading epic (#4); proposing stays in #65; the CLI/MCP
15	`propose` face stays in #44. This module owns only the check phase and its typed
16	result, `PropertyCheckRun`, which #4 consumes (its `held()` subset is the
17	mutation-kill candidate set) and #44 serializes.
18	
19	The driver is deterministic and effect-free in itself — verification, storage, and
20	harness rendering live behind the `VerifyPort` / `PropertyStorePort` /
21	`HarnessWriterPort` seams; the only I/O it performs is materializing each harness
22	to `work_dir` (the file esbmc reads) and emitting telemetry through the injected
23	sink (default `NullSink` = no-op).
24	"""

65	class PropertyOutcome(Enum):
66	    """Per-property verdict (ADR-0009 D4).
67	
68	    `HELD`/`VIOLATED`/`UNKNOWN` mirror the ESBMC verdict on the real unit;
69	    `ERROR` (a tooling/invocation failure) and `SKIPPED` (a reachability kind,
70	    deferred per ADR-0009 D2) are added so neither is silently coerced into a
71	    code verdict. `VACUOUS` (W3.4) is added the same way: ESBMC said VERIFIED but
72	    the post-call vacuity probe could not reach the assertion at that k, so the
73	    postcondition was never evaluated and the result is not a HELD.
74	    """
75	
76	    HELD = "held"  # Verified up to k
77	    VIOLATED = "violated"  # counterexample found
78	    UNKNOWN = "unknown"  # inconclusive after the ladder is exhausted
79	    ERROR = "error"  # esbmc failed (e.g. a harness that didn't compile)
80	    SKIPPED = "skipped"  # reachability kind, deferred (ADR-0009 D2)
81	    VACUOUS = "vacuous"  # Verified, but the post-call point is unreachable at k
82

84	@dataclass(frozen=True)
85	class PropertyVerdict:
86	    """One property's outcome on the real unit — the atom grading (#4) consumes.
87	
88	    `k` is the bound the verdict settled at (`None` when `SKIPPED`); `result` is
89	    the raw typed ESBMC result (`None` when `SKIPPED`); `harness_source` is the
90	    exact harness checked, kept as provenance so #4 can re-render it against
91	    mutants. `skip_reason` explains a `SKIPPED` outcome, a render-failure `ERROR`,
92	    or a vacuity-probe `VACUOUS`/`UNKNOWN`. `probe` is the post-call probe's
93	    reading (`None` when no probe ran: anything other than a Verified verdict);
94	    on a `VACUOUS`/probe-`UNKNOWN` outcome `result` is the Verified verdict
95	    / the probe's own inconclusive result respectively, both at `k`.
96	    `length_bounds` are the ``(param, max_len)`` caps the harness applied to
97	    buffer lengths the property's domain left unconstrained, so the verdict reads
98	    as scoped to ``len <= N`` rather than to every length (empty when none).
99	    """
100	
101	    property_id: str
102	    unit_id: str
103	    kind: str  # "semantic" | "reachability"
104	    outcome: PropertyOutcome
105	    k: int | None
106	    result: EsbmcResult | None
107	    harness_source: str | None
108	    skip_reason: str | None = None
109	    length_bounds: LengthBounds = ()
110	    probe: ProbeReachability | None = None
111	
112	    @classmethod
113	    def skipped(
114	        cls, property_id: str, unit_id: str, kind: str, *, reason: str
115	    ) -> PropertyVerdict:
116	        """A deferred property (a reachability kind, ADR-0009 D2): `SKIPPED`, no
117	        `k`/`result`/`harness_source`, carrying only the `reason` it was deferred.
118	        """
119	        return cls(
120	            property_id,
121	            unit_id,
122	            kind,
123	            PropertyOutcome.SKIPPED,
124	            k=None,
125	            result=None,
126	            harness_source=None,
127	            skip_reason=reason,
128	        )
129	
130	    @classmethod
131	    def render_failed(
132	        cls, property_id: str, unit_id: str, kind: str, *, reason: str
133	    ) -> PropertyVerdict:
134	        """A property whose harness could not be rendered (#64 fail-loud
135	        `HarnessError`): `ERROR` with no `k`/`result`/`harness_source` — esbmc was
136	        never invoked — carrying the render-failure `reason`. Distinct from an
137	        esbmc-error verdict (`settled` with an `Error` result), which does have a
138	        harness and a result.
139	        """
140	        return cls(
141	            property_id,
142	            unit_id,
143	            kind,
144	            PropertyOutcome.ERROR,
145	            k=None,
146	            result=None,
147	            harness_source=None,
148	            skip_reason=reason,
149	        )

151	    @classmethod
152	    def settled(
153	        cls,
154	        property_id: str,
155	        unit_id: str,
156	        kind: str,
157	        outcome: PropertyOutcome,
158	        *,
159	        k: int | None,
160	        result: EsbmcResult,
161	        harness_source: str,
162	        length_bounds: LengthBounds = (),
163	        probe: ProbeReachability | None = None,
164	        reason: str | None = None,
165	    ) -> PropertyVerdict:
166	        """A property verified to a terminal `outcome` along the k-ladder: the
167	        settled bound `k`, the raw `result` (kept for #4 to re-render against
168	        mutants), and the exact `harness_source` checked. No `reason` — the
169	        outcome speaks for itself — except when the vacuity probe qualified it.
170	        """
171	        return cls(
172	            property_id,
173	            unit_id,
174	            kind,
175	            outcome,
176	            k=k,
177	            result=result,
178	            harness_source=harness_source,
179	            skip_reason=reason,
180	            length_bounds=length_bounds,
181	            probe=probe,
182	        )
183	
184	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
185	        """A JSON-serializable dict — the shape the grading harness (#4) reads."""
186	        return {
187	            "property_id": self.property_id,
188	            "unit_id": self.unit_id,
189	            "kind": self.kind,
190	            "outcome": self.outcome.value,
191	            "k": self.k,
192	            "harness_source": self.harness_source,
193	            "skip_reason": self.skip_reason,
194	            "probe": self.probe.value if self.probe is not None else None,
195	            "length_bounds": dict(self.length_bounds),
196	            "result": (
197	                _result_payload(self.result, self.k)
198	                if self.result is not None
199	                else None
200	            ),
201	        }

207	# reachability witness, not a coverage claim, so it is stated wherever a probed
208	# verdict is reported (transcript footer, the vacuous reason, CLI/MCP docs).
209	VACUITY_LIMITATION = (

216	@dataclass(frozen=True)
217	class PropertyCheckRun:
218	    """The result of checking every stored property for one unit."""
219	
220	    unit_id: str
221	    verdicts: tuple[PropertyVerdict, ...]
222	
223	    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
224	        """Per-outcome tally; every `PropertyOutcome` key present (0 if none)."""
225	        counts = {outcome.value: 0 for outcome in PropertyOutcome}
226	        for verdict in self.verdicts:
227	            counts[verdict.outcome.value] += 1
228	        return counts
229	
230	    def held(self) -> tuple[PropertyVerdict, ...]:
231	        """The HELD subset — the mutation-kill candidate set the #4 seam grades."""
232	        return tuple(v for v in self.verdicts if v.outcome is PropertyOutcome.HELD)
233	
234	    @property
235	    def outcome(self) -> RunOutcome:
236	        """Core-owned, worst-outcome-wins summary across every checked property.
237	
238	        `violated` > `unknown` > `error` > `empty` (nothing semantically
239	        checked: no property stored, or every stored one was `skipped`) >
240	        `held`. A `vacuous` verdict (W3.4) is folded into `unknown`: the
241	        property's postcondition was never evaluated, so it is as inconclusive
242	        as a timeout and must never read as `held`; `counts()`/`verdicts[]`
243	        still tell the two apart. The one field a caller — the CLI's exit
244	        code, the MCP `check` payload, and the composed loop (`core/loop.py`) —
245	        reads instead of re-deriving verdict severity itself (issue #213): an
246	        adapter that recomputed this from `counts()` on its own could drift from
247	        the CLI's own policy, or (CLAUDE.md "never silently pass") miss that
248	        `empty` must not read as a clean pass just because it shares `held`'s
249	        exit code.
250	        """
251	        return self._outcome_for_counts(self.counts())
252	
253	    def _outcome_for_counts(self, counts: dict[str, int]) -> RunOutcome:
254	        if counts["violated"]:
255	            return "violated"
256	        if counts["unknown"] or counts["vacuous"]:
257	            return "unknown"
258	        if counts["error"]:
259	            return "error"
260	        checked = len(self.verdicts) - counts["skipped"]
261	        if checked == 0:
262	            return "empty"
263	        return "held"
264	
265	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
266	        """A JSON-serializable dict (unit id, counts, outcome, and every verdict)."""
267	        counts = self.counts()
268	        return {
269	            "unit_id": self.unit_id,
270	            "counts": counts,
271	            "outcome": self._outcome_for_counts(counts),
272	            "verdicts": [verdict.to_dict() for verdict in self.verdicts],
273	        }

276	class SemanticHarnessWriter:
277	    """The production `HarnessWriterPort`: a thin adapter over #64's writer.
278	
279	    Adapts the driver's `Unit`/`RenderedHarness` carriers to
280	    `render_property_harness`, the properties-domain recipe that owns the harness
281	    knowledge (parse the signature from the slice -> project the property onto a
282	    `SemanticSpec` -> render). Keeping the recipe in #64 (not here) is what lets
283	    `check_properties` stay a pure driver that need not know how a stored
284	    property becomes a harness. Fail-loud: a non-renderable unit/property raises
285	    `HarnessError` rather than emit a silent mis-harness. Non-semantic properties
286	    are skipped by the driver *before* this is reached (ADR-0009 D2), so `render`
287	    only ever sees semantic ones.
288	
289	    `max_len` (default `None`: no cap) is forwarded to the harness so a
290	    `(ptr, len)` buffer the property's domain leaves unbounded is capped at
291	    ``len <= max_len`` (#299); the caps actually applied ride back on the
292	    `RenderedHarness`. A negative `max_len` is a per-property render `ERROR`
293	    (the harness's own `HarnessError`); the Core faces reject it up front.
294	    """
295	
296	    def __init__(self, max_len: int | None = None) -> None:
297	        self._max_len = max_len
298	
299	    def render(self, unit: Unit, prop: Property) -> RenderedHarness:
300	        harness = build_property_harness(
301	            unit_source=unit.source_text,
302	            symbol=unit.symbol,
303	            prop=prop,
304	            max_len=self._max_len,
305	        )
306	        return RenderedHarness(
307	            source_text=harness.source_text,
308	            length_bounds=harness.length_bounds,
309	            probe_source_text=harness.probe_source_text,
310	        )
